blurb_html: Short-grain rice cooked 1:1 with kombu, then rice vinegar, sugar and salt cut in while you fan it — glossy, separate grains for nigiri and rolls.

chips.html: 1 batch · ~660 g, 3–4 servings (2 rice-cooker cups raw)

description: Short-grain rice cooked 1:1 with kombu, then rice vinegar, sugar and salt cut in while you fan it — glossy, separate grains for nigiri and rolls.
equipment_html: Rice cooker, or a heavy pot with a tight lid
Rice-cooker cup (180 ml) or a measuring cup
Hangiri (wooden sushi tub), or a wide bowl / baking sheet
Fan, or a piece of card

intro_html: The rice under every nigiri and roll. It gets less water than plain rice because it still has to drink the seasoning, and the seasoning goes on while the rice is hot, cut in with a paddle — never stirred — while you fan off the steam.

notes.html:
• The standard sushi-zu is rice vinegar, sugar and salt — no mirin.
  • That's what Just One Cookbook, which this page follows, uses.
  • Some home cooks swap part of the sugar for mirin; I haven't found a source I trust with tested amounts, so it isn't given here.
  • If you try it, mirin is less sweet than sugar and adds liquid, so start small and taste.
notes.title_html: Is it mirin, rice vinegar and sugar?

notes.html:
• 1 rice-cooker cup (150 g raw): 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, ½ tsp kosher salt (half of the 2-cup batch — my arithmetic).
  • 2 cups (300 g raw, this page): 4 tbsp vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp kosher salt.
  • 3 cups (450 g raw): ⅓ cup (80 ml) vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar, 1½ tsp kosher salt — JOC's own 3-cup amounts, a touch milder than 1½ × the 2-cup batch.
1 rice-cooker cup of raw rice makes about 330 g cooked: roughly 16–18 nigiri at 18–20 g each, 3 inside-out rolls (110 g each) or 2 medium rolls (150 g each).

• JOC measures Diamond Crystal kosher salt, which is light and flaky.
  • With fine table or sea salt use about half the volume (my conversion).

• Seasoned rice vinegar (sushi-zu in a bottle) replaces all three: use the same volume as the plain vinegar and skip the sugar and salt.
  • Taste — some are sharper.

• A wide bowl or a damp baking sheet works.
  • The wooden tub is better because it soaks up extra moisture as the rice cools.

steps.body_html:
• Level off the rice in a rice-cooker cup (180 ml = 150 g) and tip it into a large bowl.
  • Add just enough water to cover and pour it off straight away — the dry grains drink the first, dirtiest water fastest.

steps.title: Measure and quick-rinse

steps.body_html:
• With almost no water in the bowl, swirl the grains with your fingertips for 10–15 seconds.
  • Cover with water and pour the cloudy water off at once.
  • Repeat twice more, until the water is almost clear.

steps.title: Drain well

steps.body_html:
• Put the rice in the rice-cooker bowl or pot and add the water — 1 : 1 by volume. In a rice cooker, fill to the Sushi line if it has one; on White Rice, just under the line.
  • Wipe the kombu with a damp cloth (don't rinse off the white powder — it's flavour) and lay it on top.
  • Soak 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Water and kombu, then soak

uses_rows.amount_html: 1 piece

steps.body_html:
• Rice cooker:
    • Sushi setting if it has one, otherwise White Rice.
  • Pot:
    • Lid slightly ajar, bring to a boil over medium heat.
    • Once it boils, lid on tight, low heat for 12–13 minutes. Don't lift the lid.
    • Off the heat, lid still on, 10 minutes more.
steps.title: Cook

steps.body_html:
• Warm in a small pan over medium heat, whisking:
    • rice vinegar, unseasoned 4 tbsp (60 ml)
    • sugar 2 tbsp
    • kosher salt (diamond crystal) — or half as much fine salt 1 tsp
  • Take it off as soon as the sugar has dissolved and it's nearly simmering. (Microwave: about 1 minute.)
  • Use it warm or at room temperature — cold seasoning doesn't soak in evenly.
steps.title: Make the sushi-zu

steps.body_html:
• Wet the hangiri (or a wide bowl or baking sheet) and wipe it so it's damp, not wet.
  • Lift out the kombu. Turn the hot rice into the tub and spread it out with the paddle.

steps.title: Into the tub

steps.body_html: While the rice is still hot, pour the sushi-zu over it, running it off the paddle so it spreads evenly instead of pooling in one spot.

steps.title: Pour the seasoning over the paddle

steps.body_html:
• Hold the paddle at about 45° and slice through the rice in strokes — stirring crushes the grains into paste.
  • Fan hard as you go: it drives off steam and gives the shine.
  • Every few strokes, gently turn a paddleful over.
  • Stop when the rice is glossy and about body temperature.

steps.title: Cut it in and fan

steps.body_html:
• Lay a damp towel over the rice and use it at room temperature within a few hours.
  • Not the fridge — cold makes it hard.
  • Leftovers freeze for up to a month.
